deep.reconstruction:
Context: 'Magn. Obs.', 7 December (year not given; probably the 1830s–40s Göttingen magnetometer work). The page is a field note measuring the distance r from the reading scale to the front surface of the magnetometer mirror. In the Gauss–Poggendorff mirror-and-scale method, a deflection of n scale units corresponds to an angle φ with tan(2φ) = n/r. Each scale unit is therefore worth about 1/(2r) radians, so r must be known accurately.

The distance is measured in three legs with plumb lines:
(1) Plumb thread to scale: d1 = 48.7 mm.
(2) Plumb thread to a second plumb hung in front of the hook of the rod: d2 = 4700.0 mm.
(3) Second plumb to mirror: d3 = 135.4 mm.
Sum: r = d1 + d2 + d3 = 48.7 + 4700.0 + 135.4 = 4884.1 mm.

Comparison with an earlier measurement: one made with the '3 m' rods gave 4875.2 mm, a difference of 8.9 mm. The writer explains this 'partly' by the rods being longer than 3 m. He compared the rods against the large standard measure used for today's measurement and found the intervals 0–3 m = 3002.8, 3–6 m = 3002.8 and 6–9 m = 3002.5 mm (mean about 3002.7).

Implicit step (mine): a rod that is too long makes the reading too small. The corrected earlier value is therefore about 4875.2 × 3002.7/3000 ≈ 4879.6 mm (4879.75 mm if 3002.8 is used). This removes about 4.4–4.6 mm of the 8.9 mm discrepancy, leaving about 4.4 mm unexplained. That is consistent with the word 'zum Theil' (partly).

The closing initial is unclear. It may be another observer (e.g. Weber), not necessarily Gauss.
errors: The rod-length correction explains only about half of the 8.9 mm discrepancy (corrected old value ≈ 4879.6–4879.75 mm). The text acknowledges this with 'zum Theil'; this is not an error.

results.what: Determination of the scale–mirror distance of a magnetometer by summing plumb-line segments, with calibration of 3 m measuring rods against a standard measure
results.modern_name: Calibration of the optical lever arm in the mirror-and-scale (Poggendorff–Gauss) reading method; comparison of length standards
results.usually_credited_to: Mirror reading: Poggendorff (1826) and Gauss (1832–33); routine laboratory metrology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine laboratory record from the Göttingen magnetic observatory: a simple sum of measured distances and a rod-calibration remark. It contains no mathematical content beyond addition and a proportional length correction.

checkable.asserts: Discrepancy between the new and old measurements is 8.9 mm (= 89/10)
Old measurement corrected for mean rod length ≈ 4879.6 mm, explaining only part of the discrepancy

transcription_corrections: The first line gives the value '48.7 mm' twice, once inline ('48mm,7') and once in the right column; this is the same number, not two entries.
In the bracketed illegible word before 'Maaßstabe', the image shows a struck-through word; the reading as deleted is plausible.
Final initial 'B.[?]' is uncertain; it may be another letter (e.g. 'W.'). The author of this note may not be Gauss.
